title: Grove's governance training wheels come off only when Sky decides GROVE is decentralized enough, with no stated metric
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.2.2.2.1.2.4 ends with the sunset condition for the Core Council Risk Advisor gate: "This transitionary phase will last until Sky determines that the GROVE token is decentralized enough to allow for meaningful governance by token holders."

Three features of that sentence are worth isolating. The **decider** is Sky, not Grove — the constrained party has no say in when the constraint lifts. The **standard** is qualitative ("decentralized enough" for "meaningful governance") with no threshold, no metric, and no measurement method. And there is **no deadline**, so the transitionary phase can in principle persist indefinitely without any party breaching the Artifact.

This sits in tension with the rest of the Root Edit process, which is otherwise specified with unusual precision: seven-day reviews, three-day polls, Wednesday 16:00 UTC cut-offs, 1% thresholds. The contrast suggests the vagueness is a choice rather than an oversight — a hard trigger could be gamed by manufacturing the appearance of distribution, whereas discretion cannot.

The honest reading is that GROVE holders hold conditional governance rights whose condition is controlled by a counterparty. Any assessment of Grove's decentralization has to treat the transitionary phase as the operative regime, not as a temporary deviation from the specified one.
description: The phase requiring Core Council Risk Advisor approval lasts 'until Sky determines' sufficient decentralization — an open-ended discretion held by the parent, not by GROVE holders.
